title: Is Aggregation the Only Choice? Federated Learning via Layer-wise Model Recombination

problem.claim: Unevenly distributed client data causes existing FedAvg-based federated learning methods to have low inference performance.

gap.claim: Different client data distributions produce local models with different optimization directions, so aggregating them can yield a poorly generalized global model that performs worse for most clients.

contributions.claim: FedMR is a federated learning paradigm in which the server shuffles layers from collected local models to generate multiple recombined models for client training instead of producing one aggregated global model.
FedMR aims to guide recombined models toward flat regions of the optimization landscape.
The paper theoretically analyzes the convergence of model recombination.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe FedMR as a novel federated learning paradigm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that recombined models have a higher probability of entering a flat area when local models occupy different areas.
The authors report that when recombined models occupy the same flat area, they are optimized in the same direction.
The authors report that FedMR significantly improves inference accuracy relative to state-of-the-art federated learning methods without exposing client privacy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Uneven client data distributions lead to low inference performance in existing FedAvg-based methods.
Client-specific data distributions create different local optimization directions, making aggregation poorly generalized.
FedMR recombines model layers to steer training toward flat regions rather than aggregating local models into one global model.
Layer recombination is argued to increase the chance of reaching a shared flat area and common optimization direction.
The paper provides a convergence analysis and reports improved inference accuracy without exposing client privacy.

source_observation.claim: The authors connect poor federated generalization to local models following different optimization directions under heterogeneous client data.

interpretation.claim: When averaging combines locally misaligned solutions, changing the combination structure may be an alternative to changing the aggregation weights.

application.claim: For federated optimization with heterogeneous clients, investigate structured model recombination as a complement or alternative to direct parameter aggregation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when layer-wise recombination fails or which client, model, or distribution conditions are required.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, model architectures, baselines, or numerical accuracy improvements.
The abstract does not describe the convergence assumptions or theoretical guarantees.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for layer shuffling or client training.
